teams.heading: England respond to half-time deficit by crushing Australia in Salford
teams.body: England secured a emphatic 48-15 victory over Australia in their WXV Global Series opener, recovering from an uncharacteristic 10-5 half-time deficit to extend their winning streak to 39 matches. Head coach John Mitchell praised the side's resilience, stating, "It is an absolute joke if you are worried about being down 10-5. More important is how we worked our way back into it." The win, featuring eight tries, provides momentum ahead of next weekend's clash against Canada at Sandy Park.

teams.heading: The IRFU rules out moving Ireland Six Nations games to America
teams.body: The IRFU has dismissed suggestions that it is considering relocating any Six Nations matches to the United States. Following comments from World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin, who suggested that an Ireland-Italy fixture could resonate with North American audiences, the Union issued a firm statement on Friday. The governing body confirmed there are "currently no plans or discussions" to move home games, maintaining that the opportunity for supporters to watch their teams on home soil remains central to the competition's appeal.

teams.body: The Vodafone Wales WXV Series will be broadcast on BBC One Wales and iPlayer, the WRU has confirmed. WRU Chief Commercial Officer Tomos Grace noted that women’s rugby is the "fastest growing part of the game," and this deal ensures top-quality international fixtures remain free-to-air for audiences across the nation throughout the autumn.

teams.heading: South Africa defeat New Zealand 43-28 to secure series triumph
teams.body: South Africa finished their four-Test tour on a high note, beating New Zealand 43-28 at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Saturday. The result marks a successful conclusion to the series for Rassie Erasmus’ side, who entered the fixture holding a 2-1 lead. Siya Kolisi praised the support following the win, stating, "I want to thank every single South Africa here and back at home. We are so grateful. We do it for you each and every time."
